title: Cuban Missile Crisis 1962 – Allison's three lenses (Session 7)
text: In October 1962, US reconnaissance flights discover Soviet nuclear missile sites under construction in Cuba, about 150 km from Florida. President Kennedy gathers a small crisis committee (ExComm) of advisers, cabinet members and military chiefs. Intelligence is incomplete and the missiles may soon be operational.

Options on the table range from doing nothing and diplomatic pressure to an air strike or an invasion of Cuba. The military chiefs push for an air strike; others warn of escalation to nuclear war. After about a week the US announces a naval blockade (“quarantine”) of Cuba, while negotiating secretly with Khrushchev. The Soviets finally withdraw the missiles; the US promises not to invade Cuba and later removes its missiles from Turkey.
Graham Allison (Essence of Decision, 1971) explains this decision with three models: bounded rationality, the organisational model and the political model.
